format: pala-1 scitt-bridge statement vector, construction v3
relation_to_v2: v2 (scitt-statement-vector.json) is unchanged and remains valid. v3 adds payload key 5, the derived root over records 0..last_seq, and is named by its own content type in the protected header, so a v2 verifier - which requires exactly keys 1-4 - rejects a v3 statement by type rather than misreading it.
purpose: Two v3 statements of one chain and the prefix-consistency proof between their roots. A holder of these three artifacts and no chain verifies both signatures, reads the two roots the signatures cover, and verifies that the 12-record state extends the 8-record state - the check v2 statements cannot support, because they carry heads and the proof connects roots. Real crypto, fake entropy - never use this key outside a test vector.

key.source: RFC 8032, section 7.1, TEST 1 - a published test key, chosen so nothing about it is ours

subject_chain.note: record_hash of each core-vector record, seq order - the leaves of the tree

construction.content_type_note: protected header label 3; the v2 type is application/vnd.palimpsests.pala1-head+cbor. A root under the v2 type, or the v3 type without a root, MUST be refused.
construction.payload: attached CBOR map: {1: chain head (32 bytes), 2: first_seq, 3: last_seq, 4: 'pala-1/v1.0', 5: derived root (32 bytes)}
construction.root_rule: key 5 is the PALA-1 section 4.3 tree over the record hashes of records 0..last_seq in seq order (consistency-proof.md section 1): leaf(d) = SHA-256(0x00 || d), node(l, r) = SHA-256(0x01 || l || r), an unpaired node promoted, never duplicated. ALWAYS from record 0 - it does not depend on first_seq: the later statement here reports records 8..11 (first_seq = 8) and its root covers 0..11. A root over first_seq..last_seq would connect to nothing.
construction.everything_else: exactly as v2: key, kid derivation, CWT claims, header order, tag 18

consistency.verification: RFC 9162 section 2.1.4.2 with the roots read from the two statements

tamper_expectations: flip any bit of the root inside a statement's payload: signature verification MUST fail (the payload is signed)
a root that is not the derived root over 0..last_seq of the chain: a verifier holding the chain MUST reject it
a root computed over first_seq..last_seq (here 8..11) instead of the prefix: MUST be rejected against the chain, and does not verify in the consistency proof
a root over last_seq or last_seq + 2 records instead of last_seq + 1: MUST be rejected against the chain
the v3 content type with no key 5, or key 5 under the v2 content type: MUST be refused, whatever the signature says
drop the last node of the consistency path, or swap the two roots: the proof MUST NOT verify
without the chain, a verifier reports the root as carried, not recomputed - never as verified
